_about: ENHANCEMENT E16: the on-screen touch controls' look and layout, read by game/render/TouchControls (whose built-in values are the shipped manifest's, game/data/touch_controls.json: this file names every field, so none of them applies). Replacing the art is a data-only change: put the new PNGs anywhere under game/data, point 'image' at them and adjust 'size' (what each is drawn at, stretched: these placeholders are twice it) and the placement. Keep straight alpha and no exact magenta #FF00FF (the HUD keys it out). Units are logical pixels: the logical screen is always 768 tall, 1024 wide in the menus and in 4:3 levels, wider in widescreen levels, so sizes here are already relative to the screen's height. 'anchor' is the corner of the safe area a control hangs from and 'offset' the distance from that corner to its nearest edges, inward. 'hitPadding' is how far past its edge a finger still lands on it; 'shape' (circle or rect) is its touch area. 'scale' multiplies every size, offset and padding. Alphas are 0..1: 'idleAlpha' at rest, 'pressedAlpha' while held. A control with "enabled": false is not there at all (a layout without the combo buttons, say); one left out of this file keeps its built-in place and image.
_provenance: THE FIRST, PLACEHOLDER LOOK, kept one step away: copy this file over game/data/touch_controls.json to use it (the port ships Magic Rampage's buttons, whose manifest that is). Placeholder art drawn by tools/art/make_touch_art.py (shapes only, no fonts). The layout is the port's own: the direction control under the left thumb; the actions under the right as a pad's face buttons, placed as E3 maps them (A jump at the bottom, X sword left, B fire right, Y light top); the two combo buttons in a row above them, each on its attack's side; pause and back in the top-right corner below the run's timer (setupScene.as:337 draws it at (W-50, 0)), clear of the player status frames at the top-left (interface.as). Keys starting with '_' are notes.

dpad._note: Left, right and down (K_LEFT, K_RIGHT, K_DOWN; 'downSector', as before E25); no up, which only jumps. The thumb slides without lifting; 'deadZone' is the fraction of the radius at the centre that means nothing. The arrows are drawn over the disc in the same box, each brightened while its direction is held; the knob follows the thumb, and 'atRest' true keeps it at the disc's centre with no thumb there.

swordCombo._note: The sword combo as a macro of player 1's keys, one a tick: the way the wizard faces, again after a release, then K_S (CMD side, side, SWORD; playerInput.as:361). Waits first, if need be, for the combo buffer to empty (210 ms without a press, combo.as:116).

spellCombo._note: The spell combo as a macro: K_DOWN, the way the wizard faces, then K_D (CMD DOWN, side, SPELL; playerInput.as:380).

exitDown._note: E25's down button, which this look, older than it, does without: its disc has down.

pause._note: K_ESC in a level or an arena: E13's pause

back._note: K_ESC in the arena select, game over and the end screens: back to the menu (waitForInputToMenu, escToGoToMenu). Hidden in the main menu, in the options (the original's own Back arrow is there) and in the pause.
